record.context_brief: Blurred maximal symmetry numbers on finite intervals
record.original_question: For the finite interval n = {0, 1, ..., n-1} with counting measure and integer central symmetries, let bms_r(n) be the blurred maximal symmetry number obtained by taking the infimum over measurable blurred r-colorings. Calculate the values of bms_r(n), at least for small n and for r = 2.

evidence.quote: Taking this infimum over all measurable blurred r-colorings of X, we obtain the definition of the blurred maximal symmetry number bmsr(X).
Problem 6.3. Calculate the values bmsr(n) (at least for small n and r = 2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and consider the finite interval $\mathbf{n}=\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ equipped with the counting measure $\mu$. A subset $S\subseteq\mathbf{n}$ is called symmetric if there exists a center $c\in\tfrac12\mathbb{Z}$ such that the reflection $s_c:x\mapsto 2c-x$ maps $S$ onto itself and fixes no point of $S$ pointwise other than possibly $c$ (i.e., $S$ is invariant under a non-trivial central symmetry of the ambient line that preserves $\mathbf{n}$).

For an integer $r\ge 2$, a blurred $r$-coloring of $\mathbf{n}$ is a measurable function 
$$\chi:\mathbf{n}\longrightarrow \Delta_r:=\Big\{(p_1,\dots,p_r)\in[0,1]^r:\sum_{i=1}^r p_i=1\Big\}$$
into the probability simplex; writing $\chi(x)=(\chi_1(x),\dots,\chi_r(x))$, the value $\chi_i(x)$ is interpreted as the "weight" assigned to color $i$ at the point $x$. The blurred monochromatic measure of a subset $S\subseteq\mathbf{n}$ in color $i$ is 
$$m_i(S,\chi):=\sum_{x\in S}\chi_i(x).$$

For a blurred $r$-coloring $\chi$, define
$$\sigma(\chi):=\sup_{S}\;\max_{1\le i\le r}\,m_i(S,\chi),$$
where the supremum is taken over all symmetric subsets $S\subseteq\mathbf{n}$ in the sense above. Finally, define the blurred maximal symmetry number
$$\operatorname{bms}_r(\mathbf{n}):=\inf_{\chi}\sigma(\chi),$$
where the infimum is taken over all measurable blurred $r$-colorings $\chi$ of $\mathbf{n}$.

Compute the values $\operatorname{bms}_r(\mathbf{n})$. In particular, determine $\operatorname{bms}_2(\mathbf{n})$ for as many small values of $n$ as possible, and provide either explicit formulas or sharp asymptotic estimates as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches confirm the framework of (blurred) maximal symmetry numbers introduced by Banakh and collaborators in surveys on symmetry and colorings, where the technique of blurred colorings is used to bound $\operatorname{ms}_r$ on intervals. No subsequent paper explicitly computing $\operatorname{bms}_r(\mathbf{n})$ for the finite interval (even for $r=2$ and small $n$) was located, so the status appears to remain undetermined.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry and colorings: some results and open problems, II
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys principal results and open problems related to colorings of geometric and algebraic objects endowed with symmetries, concentrating on maximal symmetry numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the framework in which the blurred maximal symmetry number bms_r is introduced and lists open problems on its computation.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry (Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximal symmetry numbers ms(Ω,r) and monochromatic symmetric subsets under r-colorings.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background on ms_r but does not compute bms_r(n) for the finite interval.
